newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DALLAS ROOKIE TURNS BACK DETROIT FOR 2-1 VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DALLAS ROOKIE TURNS BACK DETROIT FOR 2-1 VICTORY.

text.p: Roman Turek made 38 saves for his second career victory and Brent Gilchrist and Mike Modano scored power-play goals, leading the Dallas Stars to a 2-1 win over the Detroit Red Wings on Friday.
Turek, making just his second NHL start, stopped all 22 shots over the first two periods before allowing Igor Larionov's fifth goal 9:41 into the third.
"He (Turek) knows their shooters, he really knows the Russians," Stars coach Ken Hitchcock said. "We needed someone who was on top of his game tonight, that's why we went with him."
In Buffalo, Alexei Zhitnik scored with 7:53 left in the third period to lift the Buffalo Sabres into a 2-2 tie with the St. Louis Blues.

The Blues carried a 2-1 lead into the third, but Zhitnik tied it with his fourth goal of the season. He took a stride over the St. Louis blue line and unleashed a slap shot that went through the legs of defenceman Marc Bergevin and between the pads of goaltender Grant Fuhr.
Geoff Courtnall and Jim Campbell scored for the Blues.

In Ottawa, Martin Brodeur rebounded from recent shaky play to record his fourth shutout of the season, and Bill Guerin scored the game's only goal as the New Jersey Devils blanked the Ottawa Senators, 1-0.

Brodeur, who had been pulled in each of his previous two starts, faced only 19 shots for the Devils. He lasted only two periods after allowing five goals on 15 shots in Thursday's 6-1 home loss to Pittsburgh.
"I was concentrating hard, even though I didn't have many shots. When I did, I could see them and that makes it easier," Brodeur said.
At Tampa Bay, Chris Gratton scored at 8:24 of the third period to cap a three-goal comeback as the Tampa Bay Lightning defeated the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim, 3-2.
"I was hoping for something to happen with a good bounce and fortunately it bounced off one of their pads and skipped in for me," said Gratton. "I'll take those bounces any time."
Teemu Selanne and J.F. Jomphe scored to give Anaheim a 2-0 lead 7:45 into the game.

In Washington, Olaf Kolzig stopped 22 shots for his first career shutout and Michal Pivonka and Peter Bondra each had a goal and an assist, leading the Washington Capitals to a 3-0 whitewash of the Phoenix Coyotes.
Chris Simon scored the other goal for Washington. Darcy Wakaluk made 21 saves for the Coyotes.
Bondra closed the scoring with a power-play tally, his 23rd, 76 seconds into the third period.
In Edmonton, Boris Mironov's power-play goal with 14:07 remaining broke a third-period tie and lifted the Edmonton Oilers to their third straight win, 4-3 over the Toronto Maple Leafs.
The goal came 29 seconds after Doug Gilmour beat Curtis Joseph with a 30-foot slapper for a shorthanded goal, his second of the game.
